discoveries.headline: France says no to declaring your own crypto wallets
discoveries.why: France's Senate has voted down a plan that would have made people declare self-custodied crypto worth more than €100,000 on their tax returns. Holders had warned that such a list could put them at risk in a country hit by more than 70 crypto-linked kidnappings in the first eight months of 2026, and the government argued that EU DAC8 rules already bring transparency. A clear look at how privacy, safety and tax rules collide. Education, not advice.

discoveries.headline: Taiwan votes today for its mayors
discoveries.why: Taiwan goes to the polls today in local elections, and Focus Taiwan's reporters followed the last days of campaigning. The big races include New Taipei, where the KMT's Lee Shu-chuan faces the DPP's Su Chiao-hui, and Taipei, where Mayor Chiang Wan-an is up against the DPP's Puma Shen. A quick, on-the-ground guide to who is running before the results come in.
discoveries.meta_credit: Focus Taiwan · Tsao Ya-yen, Yeh Chen-yun, Liu Chien-pang, Kuo Hsuan-wen and Sean Lin

discoveries.headline: A giant mound-builder bird from the hobbit cave
discoveries.why: One lower leg bone dug up at Liang Bua cave on Flores, the home of Homo floresiensis, has revealed a new extinct megapode, Megapodius rokusi. It weighed about 3.9 kg, several times more than the orange-footed megapode that still lives on Flores, and lived roughly 190,000 to 120,000 years ago. Enrico de Lazaro explains the find by Hanneke Meijer and colleagues, named for Indonesian zooarchaeologist Rokus Due Awe.

discoveries.headline: Matthieu Ricard: happiness is a skill you can train
discoveries.why: Buddhist monk Matthieu Ricard tells Krista Tippett that happiness is not constant pleasure, which he calls "more like a recipe for exhaustion", but a way of being that gives you the resources to meet life's ups and downs. He explains how jealousy, hatred and arrogance poison our happiness, and how warmth and compassion can be cultivated like learning the piano. A calm, hopeful listen for a slow Saturday morning.
discoveries.meta_credit: On Being · Becoming Wise, with Krista Tippett

discoveries.headline: Where do animals go in winter?
discoveries.why: For thousands of years European scientists could not work out where animals vanished to each winter. Radiolab's Latif Nasser and Molly Webster revisit a 2019 favourite with Robert Krulwich, visiting a Bavarian farm with an 11-year-old and following warblers and wildebeest around the globe. Forty-five minutes of wonder for a weekend walk.
discoveries.meta_credit: Radiolab · WNYC Studios, with Latif Nasser and Molly Webster

discoveries.headline: Party Dozen's 21 Bum Salute is out now
discoveries.why: Saxophonist Kirsty Tickle and drummer Jonathan Boulet, the duo behind Party Dozen, recorded, mixed and mastered their new album 21 Bum Salute themselves, ten tracks out on City Slang. Tickle told Stereogum it is "kind of putting a middle finger up and waving at someone with a smile at the same time". A great pick for a Saturday listen, starting with "Euro Stomper".

discoveries.headline: The quiet spirituality of daily self-care
discoveries.why: Ayurvedic practitioner Adena Rose Bright explains why she sees dinacharya, the Ayurvedic daily routine, as one of the most potent tools we have for living in step with nature. She walks through her favourite ritual, abhyanga, a warm oil self-massage, and how caring for the body can open the way to meditation and to more compassion for others. General information, not medical advice.

discoveries.headline: Sun salutations, one step at a time
discoveries.why: Occupational therapist and yoga teacher Lynda Robinson breaks the classic sun salutation into its 12 poses, with gentler options such as cat and cow for the harder ones. She says it can be done in five or 15 minutes, which makes it a lovely ritual to greet the day. If you have a heart condition or a history of stroke, check with your clinician first.
discoveries.meta_credit: Cleveland Clinic Health Essentials · with Lynda Robinson, OT/L, RYT-500

discoveries.headline: Twelve lifts to build your strength from day one
discoveries.why: StrengthLog's Andreas Abelsson picks the strength exercises most worth learning first, from push-ups, rows and the overhead press to squats, lunges and deadlifts. Many come with easier versions, such as wall and kneeling push-ups, so you can start where you are and build up. Check with your clinician before starting a new program.
